description.narrative: The Project involves the development, design, construction and operation of a 1,600MW Combined Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT) power project located approximately 150 km south of the capital city of Tashkent in the Syrdarya region in Uzbekistan. The Project will be an Independent Power Producer (IPP), implemented on a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer basis, selling its generation to the state-owned JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan (NEGU), under a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement. Gas for the Project will be procured from the state owned JSC Uztransgaz under a tolling-mechanism.

The Project will constitute a strategic asset in Uzbekistan's energy mix and is expected to add cost-efficient baseload capacity to NEGU to meet the growing demand for electricity. The Project would also reduce carbon emissions in line with Uzbekistan's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) by displacing existing aging generation units with a more efficient CCGT technology. The Project would contribute to increase the resilience of electricity supply by adding installed capacity to the energy mix, and stabilize baseload supply to provide the necessary system flexibility to scale up renewable energy generation in line with Uzbekistan's carbon neutrality roadmap. The Project could also improve sector competitiveness by reinforcing market structure with increased IPP participation.
